title: Apple confirms some iPhone Duo screen problems after launch
summary: Apple confirms some iPhone Duo screen problems after launch
detailed: Apple’s first foldable iPhone has barely reached customers, and some owners are already dealing with cracked screens.
Multiple iPhone Duo owners have reported cracks developing along the center of the inner display.

In a statement provided to news outlets, the company said: “We are aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units.” Apple has instructed affected owners to contact AppleCare for a replacement.
Although iFixit found that the iPhone Duo was more repairable than other foldable phones it had tested, replacing its inner display remains complicated.
sentences: Apple’s first foldable iPhone has barely reached customers, and some owners are already dealing with cracked screens.
The iPhone Duo launched on Oct.
23 with a starting price of $1,999.
Within hours, complaints began appearing online from people who said their new phones developed cracks along the folding display.
Even more concerning, several reports describe damage appearing in nearly the same location.
Some owners say their phones made unusual noises before the screens failed.
Others noticed bright white lines spreading across the display.
Now Apple has acknowledged the issue and says affected customers can request replacements.
However, the company has yet to explain exactly what’s causing the failures.

Apple spent years developing its first folding iPhone.
The device opens to reveal a 7.6-inch display, giving people a much larger screen without carrying a separate tablet.
When closed, it looks like a compact smartphone with a 5.4-inch outer display.
The design generated enormous excitement when Apple introduced it in September .
However, that excitement took an unexpected turn shortly after the first phones reached customers.
Multiple iPhone Duo owners have reported cracks developing along the center of the inner display.
In several cases, a bright line of damaged pixels extended from the fold toward the right side of the screen.
Some owners have shared photos of the damage on Reddit, along with accounts of how quickly their new phones failed.
One owner, u/leftyhyzer16, said the screen cracked before setup was complete, after opening and closing the phone only a few times.
Another owner, u/Midnight_Slump, reported a failure within six hours and received a replacement from Apple.
Reddit moderators also checked additional photos and Apple paperwork provided by the owner.
They confirmed the damaged phone and its replacement were genuine.
Meanwhile, u/chimchambam said the display failed after just three hours.
That owner reported being turned away by an Apple Store before ultimately returning the phone through Verizon.
All three owners described problems appearing after very little use.
Their experiences don’t tell us how widespread the issue is, but they help explain why these early screen failures are getting so much attention.
26, Apple acknowledged reports about the damaged displays.

In a statement provided to news outlets, the company said: “We are aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units.” Apple has instructed affected owners to contact AppleCare for a replacement.
That’s encouraging news for anyone whose new phone has already failed, especially considering its $1,999 starting price.
However, Apple hasn’t disclosed exactly how many devices are affected or identified what’s causing the screens to crack.
We also don’t know whether the problem involves a manufacturing defect affecting certain phones or something in the overall design.
We reached out to Apple for additional comment but did not receive a response before our deadline.
Here’s what caught my attention.
Several of the damaged screens appear to crack near the hinge, right where the phone folds.
That’s a pretty troubling place for something to go wrong on a $2,000 folding phone.
The repair experts at iFixit took the iPhone Duo apart and used CT scans to get a closer look at its hinge.
They spotted something that could help explain the damage.
A small support bar may not move far enough out of the way when the phone folds.
If the display presses against that bar, it could put enough pressure on the screen to cause a crack.
This is still a theory. iFixit hasn’t confirmed that the support bar caused the reported damage, and Apple hasn’t explained what’s going wrong.
But it does raise questions about how well the hinge and flexible screen work together, especially when people are already reporting similar cracks just days after buying the phone.
Here’s another detail that caught my attention.
Although iFixit found that the iPhone Duo was more repairable than other foldable phones it had tested, replacing its inner display remains complicated.
The company gave the device a provisional repairability score of 5 out of 10.
More importantly, it reported that an out-of-warranty inner-screen repair costs $999.
That’s roughly half the starting price of the phone.
Fortunately, Apple says customers affected by this particular display issue should contact AppleCare for a replacement.
An AppleCare+ subscription is not required to request help for the acknowledged defect.
However, accidental damage and unrelated screen repairs may fall under different coverage terms.
You can learn more in our guide to checking your Apple warranty and what it covers.
If you recently purchased an iPhone Duo, pay attention to how the hinge feels when you open and close the device.
A sudden increase in resistance or an unfamiliar popping sound deserves attention.
If you notice something unusual, avoid forcing the phone open or closed.
Don’t repeatedly fold it to see whether the problem happens again.
If your screen develops cracks or bright lines, here are some steps worth taking.
Ask about replacement availability.
